newsitem.title: USA: Owensboro says switches optional soybeans to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Owensboro says switches optional soybeans to U.S..

text.p: Owensboro Grain Co has switched most of its optional purchase of soybeans to U.S. origin, a company official said.
In March, Owensboro Grain confirmed they bought about 150,000 tonnes of optional-origin soybeans for May, June and July shipment.

The first vessel from Brazil carrying about 1.8 million bushels or one Panamax cargo of 50,000 to 55,000 tonnes had arrived at the U.S. Gulf last week. It was now enroute to the plant in Owensboro, Kentucky, to be processed, the official, who asked not to be identified, said.
But the two outstanding cargoes of soybeans, each of about 1.8 million bushels, slated for June and July, would now be of U.S. origin and not from Brazil, the official said.
"We did not have the time to cancel the first vessel but we had time to cancel the others," he said.

"We were not comfortable with Brazilian beans," he said. "We were under a time frame. We had to make a decision to go ahead and to bring them or not. So we decided to opt for U.S. origin," the official added.
Price was not an issue at this point because it was already established. The company knew what the price would be for soybeans from Brazil and U.S. origin, he said.
Asked if quality was an issue, he replied the quality of Brazil's soybeans was supposed to be better than beans from the United States.
But until "we actually process them, we won't know that," he said, referring to the first cargo of Brazilian beans.
